subject: Tiered commit offsets and phased SLA offer for Dedicated migration
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tiered commit offsets and phased SLA offer for Dedicated migration

Hi Samantha / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation last week — appreciate the clarity on your seasonal peaks and the Q1 forecasting window. Per our ask, I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table for migrating a portion of your Hosted usage into a Dedicated GPU pool with a time-limited offset program to reduce migration cost risk. High level: 

- Commit tiers: 3 levels (Small / Mid / Large) mapped to reserved GPU-hours per month.
- Conversion offset: a time-limited credit applied to your first N months of Dedicated billing, sized by the tier (higher tiers get larger percentage offsets).
- Bridge months: a 3-month short-term bridge is our standard path to smooth the delta while you ramp model throughput.
- Phased SLA: throughput & latency guarantees increase over a 90-day ramp (we'll provide escalating SLAs tied to committed utilization).

Attached: ACME_migration_term_sheet_v2.pdf and a throughput_sla_table.xlsx that shows example pool sizes and expected p95 latency at different sequence lengths.

Quick example (illustrative):
- Mid tier commit (32 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day): 12-month reserved commit, 3-month conversion offset = 25% credit on Dedicated invoices months 1–3, then 5% ongoing account credit applied to months 4–12 if committed utilization >= 70%.
- SLA: Month 1: 95th p50 latency SLO with best-effort throughput. Month 2: 99th p95 SLO at 75% of committed throughput. Month 3+: full throughput guarantee at committed levels.

We can adjust the bridge length and offset sizing if you need a longer runway; this proposal is intentionally conservative so you can see the math. Would you like a short call tomorrow to walk the spreadsheet and anchor the final numbers?

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachment: ACME_migration_term_sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet, 3 pages)
Attachment: throughput_sla_table.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Analytics Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tiered commit offsets and phased SLA offer for Dedicated migration

Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample numbers. A few clarifying Qs before we escalate to finance: 

1) GPU pool sizing & burst: if our Q1 peaks are 2.2x baseline, do we need to buy for peak or is there an agreed burst policy? How are burst credits priced?
2) Commitment true-up: what happens if we exceed commit consistently in months 4–6? Are there overage rates or automatic true-up charges?
3) The phased SLA language is helpful — can you share precise latency/availability targets and any remedy credits if you miss them?
4) SOC2 and retention: procurement asked to confirm you can provide SOC 2 Type II report and clarify audit-log retention for the first 12 months post-migration.

Also — could you produce a tight worked example with actual dollar math for the mid tier (the 32 GPU-hour/day example) showing Hosted baseline costs versus Dedicated + offset for months 1–12? That will speed internal approvals.

If you can get that over by EOD Friday I can take to the procurement committee next Tuesday.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Analytics

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tiered commit offsets and phased SLA offer for Dedicated migration

Samantha — great questions, answered inline and attached a worked example: throughput_sla_table.xlsx contains the pool sizing math and the attached ACME_migration_term_sheet_v2.pdf now includes a mid-tier worked dollar example. Key points: 

1) Burst policy: we offer a built-in burst buffer equal to 30% of committed pool for months 1–3 at no additional upfront cost; sustained usage above commit + buffer will be billed at the published overage rate (0.28 per GPU-hour for Mid tier). For high-variance customers we recommend brief burst buy-ins for predictable seasonal windows — we can include 2 dedicated burst-days per quarter as a concession in the term if desired.

2) True-up / overage handling: months 4–12 automatically trigger incremental true-ups at the end of each billing period if average monthly utilization > 110% of commit; true-up invoices are priced at a reduced overage bracket (0.22 per GPU-hour) and count toward next period's utilization baseline for true-up calculations.

3) SLA specifics & credits: attached spreadsheet lists p50/p95 token latency targets and availability targets by phase. If we miss a phase SLA we apply service credits as a percentage of that month's Dedicated invoice (5% credit for phase 1 miss, 10% for phase 2, 15% for full-commit misses). Full terms are in the term sheet.

4) SOC 2 & logs: we can provide SOC 2 Type II (we'll share a redacted report); audit logs and request traces for the migration window are retained for 18 months by default for Dedicated customers (we can reduce to 12 months on request).

Attached: ACME_migration_term_sheet_v2.pdf (updated with worked example), throughput_sla_table.xlsx (worked math and latency matrix). Also dropping a DocuSign link to the current term so procurement can review: https://docusign.com/ACME-DED-2026-09.

If this looks good I can get legal to hard-stop the overage brackets and add the 2 quarterly burst-days concession we mentioned. Happy to take 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the spreadsheet and finalize numbers.

Best,
Markus
Attachment: ACME_migration_term_sheet_v2.pdf
Attachment: throughput_sla_table.xlsx
Related link: https://docusign.com/ACME-DED-2026-09

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Tiered commit offsets and phased SLA offer for Dedicated migration

Camila / Marissa — forwarding Acme thread and Markus' worked example. Legal will need to confirm the credit ladder; finance asked for a small tweak: reduce month-1 conversion offset from 25% to 20% if we buy down the overage rate to 0.20 for months 4–12 (they want better long-term yield). Highlighted the rows in throughput_sla_table.xlsx.

My recommendation: accept finance's swap (20% month-1 offset + 0.20 overage) but add a performance kicker: if utilization > 90% for months 4–6 we convert the account to a 10% additional rebate for months 7–12. That helps protect margins while giving Acme upside.

Please confirm you can sign off so I can send a clean term back to Samantha.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

- The 3-month bridge still includes the 30% burst buffer for months 1–3.
